'''Catherine Patricia Foley''' (born 10 October 1957) is an Australian [[physicist]]. She was the [[Chief Scientist of Australia]] from January 2021 to December 2024,<ref name="McCulloch">{{cite news|last1=McCulloch|first1=Daniel|date=9 November 2020|title=Cathy Foley appointed next chief scientist|work=[[Canberra Times]]|url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7003573/cathy-foley-appointed-next-chief-scientist/?cs=14264|access-date=9 November 2020|archive-date=13 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201113193420/https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/7003573/cathy-foley-appointed-next-chief-scientist/?cs=14264|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Smith 2020">{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Belinda|date=9 November 2020|title=Physicist Cathy Foley appointed Australia's next chief scientist|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/science/2020-11-09/dr-cathy-foley-appointed-australias-chief-scientist/12862742|access-date=9 November 2020|website=ABC News|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation|archive-date=9 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109032526/https://www.abc.net.au/news/science/2020-11-09/dr-cathy-foley-appointed-australias-chief-scientist/12862742|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Board">{{cite press release |url=https://www.industry.gov.au/news/dr-cathy-foley-ends-term-australias-chief-scientist |access-date=28 January 2025 |date=9 January 2025 |title=Dr Cathy Foley ends term as Australia's Chief Scientist |archive-date=28 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250128110224/https://www.industry.gov.au/news/dr-cathy-foley-ends-term-australias-chief-scientist |url-status=live}}</ref> before which she had been the chief scientist for the [[Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation]] (CSIRO) since August 2018.<ref name="Appoint">{{Cite press release|publisher=CSIRO|title=CSIRO Chief Scientist Dr Cathy Foley to be next Australian Chief Scientist|url=https://www.csiro.au/en/news/All/News/2020/November/CSIRO-Chief-Scientist-Dr-Cathy-Foley-to-be-next-Australian-Chief-Scientist|access-date=2021-07-29|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250128111853/https://www.csiro.au/en/news/All/News/2020/November/CSIRO-Chief-Scientist-Dr-Cathy-Foley-to-be-next-Australian-Chief-Scientist|first=Larry|last=Marshall|archive-date=28 January 2025|date=9 January 2020}}</ref>

Foley's research is in [[solid-state physics]] and its applications in [[superconductivity]], combining [[Materials science|material science]], [[Quantum mechanics|quantum physics]], and research translation.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cathy Foley|url=https://www.science.org.au/profile/cathy-foley|access-date=2020-08-17|website=www.science.org.au|language=en|archive-date=21 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200921095208/https://www.science.org.au/profile/cathy-foley|url-status=live}}</ref> In addition to her research science, she has also contributed significantly to the advancement of women in physics, and to professional scientific organisations.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Queen's Birthday honours for five Academy Fellows {{!}} Australian Academy of Science|url=https://www.science.org.au/news-and-events/news-and-media-releases/queens-birthday-honours-five-academy-fellows|date=8 June 2020|archive-date=28 January 2025|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250128115032/https://www.science.org.au/news-and-events/news-and-media-releases/queens-birthday-honours-five-academy-fellows|quote=Dr Cathy Foley AO PSM FAA FTSE is recognised for distinguished service to research science, to the advancement of women in physics and to professional scientific organisations. Dr Foley was elected a Fellow of the Academy this year.|access-date=2020-08-17|website=www.science.org.au|language=en}}</ref>

Foley and her group at CSIRO have performed pioneering work on [[SQUID]] systems for geomagnetic exploration of minerals, which were transitioned to industry and resulted in the discovery of mineral ores worth many billions of dollars.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://snf.ieeecsc.org/pages/abc-science-news-article-cathy-foley-csiro |title=ABC Science news article on Cathy Foley, CSIRO |access-date=13 December 2014 |archive-date=13 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213072338/http://snf.ieeecsc.org/pages/abc-science-news-article-cathy-foley-csiro |url-status=dead }}</ref> Upon Foley's appointment as Chief Scientist, the CSIRO stated: "Among her many achievements, her team’s breakthrough work in ‘SQUID’ systems for mineral exploration were commercialised in LANDTEM technology, which has led to mineral discoveries worth more than $6 billion."<ref name="Appoint" />

==Early life and education==
Catherine Patricia Foley was born on 10 October 1957<ref name=":0" /> in [[Darlinghurst]].<ref name="wwia2020">{{cite book |title=Who's Who in Australia |date=2020 |publisher=ConnectWeb}}</ref>{{page needed|date=January 2025}}

Catherine was a high school student at [[Santa Sabina College]], Strathfield. She then attended [[Macquarie University]] for her undergraduate degrees, studying for Diploma of Education in high school physics (1979) and a Bachelor of Science majoring in physics (1980). She remained at Macquarie to do a PhD in physics (1984) investigating [[indium nitride]], under the supervision of Trevor Tansley. She also spent six months on a scholarship as a research fellow, the Department of Electrical Engineering, at [[Oregon State University]], US, in [[Corvallis, Oregon|Corvallis]] while writing up her PhD.<ref name=":0" />

==Career==
In December 2024, she was appointed to the [[Australian Museum]] Trust.<ref>{{cite web|type=Ministerial media release |access-date=12 December 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250710195203/https://www.nsw.gov.au/departments-and-agencies/dciths/ministerial-media-releases/new-leadership-at-nsw-cultural-institutions |url=https://www.nsw.gov.au/departments-and-agencies/dciths/ministerial-media-releases/new-leadership-at-nsw-cultural-institutions |publisher=[[NSW Government]] |title=New leadership at NSW Cultural Institutions |author=[[Minister for the Arts (New South Wales)|Minister for the Arts]] |archive-date=10 July 2025 |url-status=live |date=10 December 2024}}</ref>

===CSIRO===
Foley joined CSIRO in 1985 as a national [[research fellow]] and was promoted to senior research scientist in 1991, [[Chief scientific officer#:~:text=A chief science officer (C.S.O., performing significant scientific research projects|principal research scientist]] in 1996, senior principal research scientist in 2000, and chief research scientist in 2008.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2013-07-17|title=Catherine Patricia (Cathy) Foley|url=https://csiropedia.csiro.au/foley-catherine-patricia/|first=Colin|last=Ward|access-date=2020-08-17|publisher=CSIROpedia|language=en-AU|archive-date=21 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200921084355/https://csiropedia.csiro.au/Foley-Catherine-Patricia/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Cathy Foley|url=https://scienceandtechnologyaustralia.org.au/profile/cathy-foley/|access-date=2020-08-17|website=Science and Technology Australia|language=en-AU}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-10-28|title=Research Scientist Classification|url=https://www.psc.nsw.gov.au/workforce-management/workforce-management-tools/research-scientist-classification|access-date=2021-07-29|website=NSW Public Service Commission|language=en-AU|archive-date=4 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804000605/https://www.psc.nsw.gov.au/workforce-management/workforce-management-tools/research-scientist-classification|url-status=live}}</ref> Dr Foley was also previously the deputy director of CSIRO's manufacturing business unit, as well as chief of the Division of Materials Science and Engineering in 2011 CSIRO's Materials Science and Engineering division.<ref>{{Cite web|last=CSIRO|title=Physicist appointed as CSIRO Chief Scientist|url=https://www.csiro.au/en/News/News-releases/2018/Physicist-appointed-as-CSIRO-Chief-Scientist|access-date=2020-08-17|website=www.csiro.au|language=en-AU}}</ref>

Foley joined the editorial board of the physics journal ''[[Superconductor Science and Technology]]'' in 2003<ref name=":0" /> and subsequently became its editor-in-chief.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2014-07-17|title=Editor-in-Chief of Superconductor Science and Technology awarded IEEE Award|url=https://ioppublishing.org/news/editor-in-chief-of-superconductor-science-and-technology-awarded-ieee-award/|access-date=2021-10-16|website=IOP Publishing|language=en-US|archive-date=1 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230701002445/https://ioppublishing.org/news/editor-in-chief-of-superconductor-science-and-technology-awarded-ieee-award/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Editorial Board - Superconductor Science and Technology|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/journal/0953-2048/page/Editorial%20Board|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-16|website=iopscience.iop.org|publisher=IOPscience|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506000009/https://iopscience.iop.org/journal/0953-2048/page/Editorial%20Board |archive-date=6 May 2021 }}</ref>

Following her departure from the role of Chief Scientist, Foley was appointed to the [[Board of directors|board]] of the CSIRO.<ref>{{cite press release |url=https://www.csiro.au/en/news/All/News/2025/January/Dr-Cathy-Foley-joins-CSIRO-Board |publisher=CSIRO |access-date=28 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250128110519/https://www.csiro.au/en/news/All/News/2025/January/Dr-Cathy-Foley-joins-CSIRO-Board |archive-date=28 January 2025 |date=3 January 2025 |title=Dr Cathy Foley joins CSIRO Board |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Office of the Chief Scientist ===
On 1 January 2021, Foley replaced [[Alan Finkel]] as [[Chief Scientist of Australia]].<ref name="McCulloch" /> She has stated as priorities: development of a national Open Access strategy, supporting emerging technologies (including establishing a working group for quantum technologies), strengthening the role of the National Science & Technology Council in advising the Government, and increasing understanding of scientific capability across Australian public service.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chief Scientist Workplan|url=https://www.chiefscientist.gov.au/workplan|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-16|website=www.chiefscientist.gov.au|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211016101551/https://www.chiefscientist.gov.au/workplan |archive-date=16 October 2021 }}</ref>

On 31 January 2024, she left this role and later took up a position on the board of the CSIRO.<ref name="Board" />

== Research ==
Foley made significant contributions to the comprehension of [[Superconductivity|superconducting materials]] and to the evolution of devices that use superconductors to detect magnetic fields and locate deposits of minerals.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Foley|first=Cathy|title=Director's Colloquium - How a single grain boundary found billions of dollars of mineral deposits: An overview of the use of SQUIDs for mineral exploration|url=https://physics.anu.edu.au/news_events/?EventID=72|url-status=live|access-date=2021-07-29|website=physics.anu.edu.au|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210325134227/https://physics.anu.edu.au/news_events/?EventID=72 |archive-date=25 March 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-02-03|title=Dr Cathy Foley, Chief Scientist of CSIRO|url=https://www.rd-alliance.org/about/organization/key-profiles/dr-cathy-foley-chief-scientist-csiro|access-date=2020-08-17|website=RDA|language=en|archive-date=19 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200319045535/https://www.rd-alliance.org/about/organization/key-profiles/dr-cathy-foley-chief-scientist-csiro|url-status=live}}</ref>

At Macquarie University, Foley and Tansley authored a series of highly regarded papers on indium nitride semiconductor films.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Tansley|first1=T. L.|last2=Foley|first2=C. P.|year=1986|title=Optical band gap of indium nitride|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|publisher=AIP Publishing|volume=59|issue=9|pages=3241–3244|doi=10.1063/1.336906|bibcode=1986JAP....59.3241T |issn=0021-8979}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Tansley|first1=T.L.|last2=Foley|first2=C.P.|year=1984|title=Electron mobility in indium nitride|journal=Electronics Letters|publisher=Institution of Engineering and Technology (IET)|volume=20|issue=25–26|pages=1066–1068|doi=10.1049/el:19840729|bibcode=1984ElL....20.1066T |issn=0013-5194}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Foley|first1=C. P.|last2=Tansley|first2=T. L.|date=1986-01-15|title=Pseudopotential band structure of indium nitride|journal=Physical Review B|publisher=American Physical Society (APS)|volume=33|issue=2|pages=1430–1433|doi=10.1103/physrevb.33.1430|pmid=9938421|bibcode=1986PhRvB..33.1430F |issn=0163-1829}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Tansley|first1=T. L.|last2=Foley|first2=C. P.|date=1986-09-15|title=Infrared absorption in indium nitride|journal=Journal of Applied Physics|publisher=AIP Publishing|volume=60|issue=6|pages=2092–2095|doi=10.1063/1.337213|bibcode=1986JAP....60.2092T |issn=0021-8979}}</ref> The work of Tansley and Dr Foley is considered central to the development of [[diode laser|semiconductor lasers]] in the blue-green region of the spectrum.

Subsequently, her work at CSIRO led to the development of high-temperature superconducting [[Josephson effect|Josephson junctions]] used in high-sensitivity magnetic field detectors used in applications such as underground deep mineral deposit detection.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr Cathy Foley|url=https://www.chiefscientist.gov.au/DrCathyFoley|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-16|website=www.chiefscientist.gov.au|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210105111314/https://www.chiefscientist.gov.au/drcathyfoley |archive-date=5 January 2021 }}</ref>

==Awards and accomplishments==
Foley's awards include the 2015 Australian Academy of Science's [[Clunies-Ross Award]], the 2013 Premier's Award for Woman of the Year, and in 2011 the AUSIMM MIOTA prize.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.women.nsw.gov.au/women_of_the_year_awards/2013_women_of_the_year_awards |title=Women NSW - 2013 Women of the Year Awards |access-date=2014-12-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141215111908/http://www.women.nsw.gov.au/women_of_the_year_awards/2013_women_of_the_year_awards |archive-date=2014-12-15 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Preceding this award, she was a fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] in the UK, past president of the [[Australian Institute of Physics]], and a fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering]] (ASTE).<ref name="Archived copy"/> She has been president of [[Science & Technology Australia|Science and Technology Australia]], where she represented 68,000 Australian scientists and technologists.<ref name="Archived copy">{{Cite web |url=https://www.questacon.edu.au/business/staff-management-and-council/bio-dr-cathy-foley |title=Bio - Dr Cathy Foley |publisher=[[Questacon]] |access-date=2014-12-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213061058/https://www.questacon.edu.au/business/staff-management-and-council/bio-dr-cathy-foley |archive-date=2014-12-13 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Foley was awarded a public service medal on [[Australia Day]] in 2003 and in the same year won the [[Eureka Prize#2003|Eureka Prize]] for the promotion of science.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2000 - 2009 Eureka Prize winners |url=https://australian.museum/get-involved/eureka-prizes/eureka-prizes-archive/eureka-prize-winners-2000s/ |website=[[Australian Museum]]}}</ref> She sits on the Scientific Advisory Committee of Australia's [[FLEET: ARC Centre of Excellence in Future Low-Energy Electronics Technologies|Centre for Future Low-Energy Electronics Technologies]].<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://www.fleet.org.au/team/?mgc_91=92/advisory-committees&mgi_91=2416/cathy-foley|title = Dr Foley biography|date = |access-date = 9 November 2017|website = Centre for Future Low-Energy Electronics Technologies|publisher = |archive-date = 9 November 2017|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171109081007/http://www.fleet.org.au/team/?mgc_91=92/advisory-committees&mgi_91=2416/cathy-foley|url-status = live}}</ref>

In May 2020, Foley was elected Fellow of the [[Australian Academy of Science]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Cathy Foley|url=https://www.science.org.au/profile/cathy-foley|last=|first=|date=|website=Australian Academy of Science|language=en|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200921095208/https://www.science.org.au/profile/cathy-foley |archive-date=21 September 2020 |access-date=2020-05-25}}</ref> and in the [[2020 Queen's Birthday Honours (Australia)|2020 Queen's Birthday Honours]] she was made an [[Order of Australia|Officer of the Order of Australia]] (AO) for "distinguished service to research science, to the advancement of women in physics, and to professional scientific organisations".<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Dr Catherine Patricia Foley PSM|url=https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/2007315|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200607153220/https://honours.pmc.gov.au/honours/awards/2007315 |archive-date=7 June 2020 |access-date=2020-06-12|website=Australian Honours Search Facility, Dept of Prime Minister and Cabinet}}</ref>
